data.title: Switchboard Announces It Will Cease Operations and End Oracle Support on September 25
data.description:
Multi-chain oracle project Switchboard said on X that it will stop operating. Its core development contributor, Switchboard Technology Labs, will gradually wind down the remaining business, and all Switchboard implementations will stop maintenance immediately before remaining support ends on September 25. According to Odaily, protocols using its oracle are being asked to migrate to alternatives such as Pyth and RedStone.

Switchboard said AI has lowered the cost of building oracles in-house, while the crypto bear market has reduced the number of new blockchains and project budgets. It also said direct data partnerships, such as those between Hyperliquid and S&P data providers, suggest protocols may increasingly obtain data directly, weakening the value of third-party oracle networks.

data.title: UK Prime Minister to Meet Trump to Seek Patriot Missile Release for Ukraine
data.description: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham is set to meet U.S. President Donald Trump next week during the United Nations General Assembly. According to Sina Finance, Burnham's main goal is to persuade Trump to release Patriot air-defense missile stockpiles for delivery to Ukraine before winter, while the two sides are also expected to discuss how Europe can ease disruptions in the Middle East.

data.title: Brazil's CVM Advances Distributed Ledger Pilot for Tokenized Securities
data.description:
Brazil's securities regulator, the CVM, is moving ahead with a distributed ledger technology pilot program for tokenized securities. According to Odaily, the 60-day test will involve simulated trading only, with no real securities or investors, and may be extended by 30 days pending board approval.

The pilot is coordinated by the CVM tokenization working group and covers the full securities lifecycle, including issuance and settlement, for stocks, bonds, receivables certificates, and investment fund units.

data.title: Brazil Securities Regulator Advances 60-Day DLT Pilot for Tokenized Securities
data.description:
Brazil's securities regulator, the CVM, is moving ahead with a distributed ledger technology pilot program for tokenized securities. According to ChainCatcher, the test will involve simulated transactions only and will not include real securities or investors.

The pilot is being coordinated by the CVM tokenization working group, or GTT, and is set to run for 60 days with a possible 30-day extension. The draft still requires board approval. The scope covers most of the securities lifecycle, including issuance through settlement for stocks, bonds, receivables certificates, and investment fund units.

data.title: Fincantieri Plans 600 Million Euro Underwater Expansion as Seabed Security Gains Focus
data.description: According to CNBC, Italian shipbuilder Fincantieri announced in July plans to acquire majority stakes in four companies for around 600 million euros ($689 million) as it expands into underwater and surface drones, marine surveying and subsea communications. The article said governments and defense companies are investing more heavily in technologies for underwater surveillance and seabed protection as concerns rise over the vulnerability of cables, pipelines and other critical infrastructure. Euroatlas said it has signed more than 100 million euros in GrayShark contracts with unnamed European navies, while TeleGeography said more than 1.5 million kilometers of submarine communications cables were in service globally as of early 2026.

data.title: Bitdeer Reports 287.2 BTC Mined and Sold in Week Ending September 18
data.description: Nasdaq-listed Bitcoin mining company Bitdeer said it produced 287.2 BTC in the week ending September 18 and sold the same amount during the period. According to Odaily, the company reported net additions of zero BTC and said it still holds no Bitcoin.

data.title: AI TRENDS | Vitalik Buterin Says Local AI Is Nearing Private, High-Task Use on Strix Halo Laptop
data.description: Vitalik Buterin said local AI on his Strix Halo laptop is approaching a point where it can handle a large share of tasks while keeping personal context private. According to NS3.AI, a benchmark image showed input-processing rates of 109.82 to 373.22 tokens per second and output rates of 18.42 to 33.37 tokens per second across 10 workloads. The analysis added that wallet software still needs fixed policies, transaction assertions, and human approval before AI can control crypto assets.

data.title: Blackstone Says India Is Nearing a Turning Point for Foreign Capital
data.description: Blackstone Inc. sees India nearing a tipping point for foreign capital, according to Bloomberg. Jon Gray said the firm’s first move into India started slowly and then faced headwinds during the global financial crisis.

data.title: Cronos Community Proposes Using Product Revenue to Buy Back and Burn CRO
data.description:
Cronos community members have introduced a proposal to use product revenue to buy back and burn CRO. The proposal also outlines changes to how Cronos Labs product revenue and future staking yields would be handled.

According to Foresight News, all revenue from Ult and Cronos Launch would be used to repurchase CRO on the open market and destroy it. The process would be carried out on-chain each month, with the hash of every transaction published.

Operating, infrastructure, and other growth-related expenses would be funded by existing capital. A strategic reserve would be used to support future staking rewards for Cronos POS.

Staking rewards would continue to be distributed under the current Cronos POS parameters. As issuance declines, funds would be added from the reserve to help keep CRO staking competitive in the market.

data.title: Linera Team Says Token Sale Fell Short of Minimum Threshold, Refunds Issued
data.description:
Linera team members said the Layer 1 blockchain project’s token sale on Sonar received nearly $900,000 in commitments but failed to meet the minimum threshold required to complete the sale. According to ChainCatcher, all token sale funds have been returned to users.

The team later sought emergency financing to keep the project moving toward mainnet launch, but it was unable to raise the needed funds. It is now gradually shutting down its app and Discord community.

User point balances will remain recorded, but the team said it cannot promise any future benefits tied to those points. The team still hopes to complete protocol development and launch the app in the future.

RootData shows that Linera has raised a cumulative $12 million, with investors including a16z Crypto, GSR, Tribe Capital, Flow Traders, and Laser Digital.

data.title: China Opens Antitrust Probes Into Four Online Travel Booking Platforms
data.description:
China opened investigations into four online hotel and travel booking platforms over suspected practices that may undermine fair competition and merchants’ rights, according to Bloomberg.

The probes extend a broader regulatory crackdown on the sector.

data.title: Zcash Whale Moves $362.56 Million in ZEC, Sends $15 Million to CEX
data.description:
A Zcash whale address, t1Lyq, transferred about $362.56 million worth of ZEC overnight on September 19, according to Arkham monitoring. According to BlockBeats On-chain Detection, $15 million was deposited into a CEX, marking the address's first exchange deposit in 10 months.

Arkham said the same batch of ZEC was worth about $163.88 million 10 months ago. The whale's unrealized gains from holding ZEC since 2025 have reached about $361 million, according to Arkham.

data.title: Bitcoin Market Cap Tops Tesla, Returns to Top 15 Global Assets
data.description:
Bitcoin's market capitalization has surpassed Tesla and returned to the top 15 global assets by market value. According to ChainCatcher, Bitcoin's market cap reached about $1.63 trillion, rising 5.05% over the past 24 hours.

Tesla shares closed Friday at $364.27, down 0.53%, giving the company a market capitalization of $1.438 trillion.

data.title: STOCKS | Republicans Distance Themselves From Trump on Tariffs and Data Centers
data.description:
Republican candidates in some of the most competitive House and Senate races are distancing themselves from U.S. President Donald Trump on core agenda items, including tariffs, war with Iran, and data centers. According to Sina Finance, the moves suggest some Republicans believe parts of Trump's policy stance are hurting their election prospects.

Maine Senator Susan Collins, Kansas Senator Roger Marshall, and Nebraska Senator Pete Ricketts have recently broken with Trump on tariffs, while seven House Republicans joined Democrats this week to back a bill requiring Trump to withdraw U.S. forces involved in hostile action against Iran unless Congress authorizes war. Iowa Representatives Zach Nunn and Mariannette Miller-Meeks also voted against Trump on Iran-related issues after previously supporting him.

Some Republicans are also uneasy about Trump's recent comments on artificial intelligence regulation, data centers, and Flock Safety surveillance cameras. Ohio Senator Jon Husted said, "This is not my position," after Trump argued that communities opposing AI data centers would "fall behind and become poor."

data.title: Polymarket Seattle Mariners Option Jumps to 78.5% Amid Sharp Volatility
data.description: The probability for the Seattle Mariners option in Polymarket’s Seattle Mariners vs. Colorado Rockies market rose sharply from 63.5% one hour ago to 78.5%, a 15 percentage point increase. According to ChainCatcher, the move was tracked by Catcher Predict monitoring, which noted that related breaking news may be influencing the shift.

data.title: Lemon to Exit Brazil Over High Capital Requirements
data.description: Argentine crypto exchange Lemon said it will stop operating in Brazil because the country’s regulatory capital requirements are too high. According to ChainCatcher, the platform will end its Lemon Card service on September 30 and automatically close all Brazilian accounts on October 16. Lemon said applying for the crypto business license required by Brazil’s central bank would tie up too much capital relative to the size of its local operations, prompting the decision to leave the market.

data.title: Visa Moves to Close Credit Card Reward Loophole for Meme Token Purchases
data.description:
Visa is working to fix a loophole that allowed users to earn rewards when buying meme tokens with credit cards through Crossmint. According to Foresight News, the issue involved using merchant codes normally assigned to digital media, a category typically used for e-books, films, and music, which let cardholders receive standard credit card points or cash back.

Crypto in America said letters it reviewed showed Visa told at least one industry participant that the category was not appropriate for meme token purchases and informed processors, including Checkout.com, that the coding would no longer be accepted. Payment processors have been given a grace period to phase out the practice, which is expected to end next week. After that, such transactions must be treated as crypto asset transactions and will be subject to Visa's related restrictions.

data.title: South Korea Justice Minister Nominee Withdraws After Cabinet Reshuffle
data.description:
South Korea’s nominee for justice minister withdrew before confirmation, according to Bloomberg.

The pullout is the second ministerial nomination to be withdrawn in a week after the president reshuffled his cabinet.

data.title: Trader Boomer Adds 10,000 ETH Long Position After Taking Profit on ZEC
data.description: BlockBeats reported on September 19 that trader Boomer added a 10,000 ETH long position at an average price of $2,610 after previously taking profit on 14,300 ZEC and securing a profit of $5.237 million. According to BlockBeats On-chain Detection, his total profit on Hyperliquid has now reached $22.28 million.
